text: The access log is written locally by the DP-03 library in the schema of the service that served the read and published to rwb.decision-record.v1 from that service's outbox; P4 writes no table of P7 and the central ledger stays with P7 rwb-decision.
why: DP-03 and Architecture v5 slide 28 require a local record plus a central ledger, and the Ownership Map gives decision_log_entry to P7, so the entry can be neither shared nor written across a schema boundary.
read: DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 28 and slide 41; Ownership Map v1; ADR-022; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON
confirm: The DP-03 library owner and the ledger owner of P7 confirm the split at the contract freeze.
impact: Fixes the entry's home, the topic it is published to and the absence of any P7 table in the app and DB stories.

text: Break-glass is time-boxed and recorded: a grant ends at the earlier of the parameter window of 4 hours and the IAM group end, with no action by anyone, and every entry written while the grant is active carries the grant id and the incident reference.
why: Legacy BR5 and BR6 fix the rule and DL38 leaves the values assumed; the target keeps the rule and enforces the end on every request instead of in a job.
read: legacy RWB-E1-039 BR5 and BR6; DL38; TSD P4 v3 T6.2; rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours
confirm: The security administrator confirms the window, the marking and the banner at the SIT sign-off.
impact: Fixes the end rule, the marking of every entry written under a grant and the end time the banner shows.

text: The legacy POST /admin/break-glass is published as POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants, and the end and read operations follow the base rule at /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end and /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}.
why: The Ownership Map and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A name the grant operation only; DP-13 supplies the service base and no source names the two other paths, while the legacy criteria keep their own spelling.
read: Ownership Map v1; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A (API-P4-013); DP-13
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-access and the gateway-bff route owner confirm the two paths before the endpoint is frozen.
impact: Fixes the three paths of the grant and how the legacy criterion is read against the published operation.

text: The refusal vocabulary of the two reads and the two writes is the message set of legacy RWB-E1-039 - MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-004, MSG-P4-007, MSG-GEN-001 to MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-P7-003 - and an expired session carries the gateway-bff session envelope because no source gives a 401 business message id.
why: The legacy errors name a message id for every business refusal but none for a 401, and the platform problem envelope already covers the session failure.
read: legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 12 and 14; Architecture v5 slide 11
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-access and the gateway-bff owner confirm the 401 handling when the baseline is tagged.
impact: Closes the vocabulary of the four operations and of the alert payloads that carry a message id.

text: The only grantee of the four tables is the rwb-access login of DP-02, whose name is not in any source, and the chart and the grant script reference it by a secret and never by a literal name.
why: TSD P4 v3 and the Ownership Map fix one login per service but no source states its name, and a literal name in a script or a chart would be a credential in a file.
read: DP-02; TSD P4 v3 T6.2; Ownership Map v1; NFR-052
confirm: The platform DB owner confirms the login name at the schema hand-over and the DevOps engineer records the secret reference.
impact: Fixes the grantee of the grant script and the one credential the chart mounts.

text: The break-glass grant is one table named break_glass_grant in rwb_access, with a unique partial constraint so that a person holds at most one active grant, and the two-person rule is enforced by the application and by that constraint.
why: No source names the table or the constraint; legacy BR4, BR5 and BR9 fix the approval and the one-use rule, and the schema must be able to refuse a second active grant.
read: legacy RWB-E1-039 BR4, BR5 and BR9; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; Ownership Map v1
confirm: The ACE database engineer and the security administrator confirm the table name, its columns and the constraint before the migration is released to SIT.
impact: Fixes the table name, its columns, its index and the constraint that the grant criterion of the DB story tests.

text: The access log is partitioned by calendar month on decided_at, retained under the decision log's retention rule with the period held as a parameter row, and reduced only by a partition drop because the period is still open at DL26.
why: No source fixes the partition granularity or the period, DL26 is open, and an append-only log cannot be pruned row by row without breaking the chain.
read: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-B (DL26); Architecture v5 slide 28; legacy RWB-E1-039 BR1
confirm: The retention owner and Compliance set the period at DL26, and the platform retention job confirms the partition drop.
impact: Fixes the partition scheme, the actor and time index and the only retention action the log allows.

text: A failed access-log write pages the platform on-call queue with MSG-P7-003 and a refused write is counted with MSG-P4-002 without a page, a break-glass activation or refusal routes to the security administrator queue with MSG-P4-004 or MSG-P4-007, and the thresholds, the topology values and the secret names are deployment values and store references rather than chart literals.
why: The legacy story names the platform administrator queue, the review by the security administrator and an incident but no route, threshold or alert rule, and TSD P4 v3 T-B leaves the non-functional targets open under DL11.
read: legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 5, 10 and 14; Architecture v5 slides 20, 30 and 42; TSD P4 v3 T5.1 and appendix T-B (DL11)
confirm: The platform on-call rota and the security administrator accept the two routes and the thresholds before the SIT release.
impact: Fixes the six alert rules, their two routes, the values they read and the six runbook entries.
